title: Nosebleed with an INR of 9 — prioritise the dangerous decision

blocks.text: Nosebleed with an INR of 9 — prioritise the dangerous decision

AMaC MRCP PACES23 • Round 5 • R5-234 • Station 2: Consultation (acute presentation) • 20 minutes • Skills A–G (clinical examination as indicated) • 14 October 2026 • Unofficial educational marking descriptors

A 76-year-old taking warfarin for atrial fibrillation attends with persistent epistaxis and an INR of 9. They began an antibiotic three days ago. Assess bleeding severity and explain the treatment plan. Take a focused history, assess immediate safety and agree the initial management with the patient or caller.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text: HOOK: Warfarin-associated over-anticoagulation with active epistaxis; severity must be graded before choosing reversal.

TRAP: Do not use an asymptomatic-INR algorithm when bleeding is present; do not treat a major bleed with oral vitamin K alone. Identify interacting antibiotics and communicate why warfarin is temporarily withheld.

rows: “I need to check whether you need urgent help.”

Do not use an asymptomatic-INR algorithm when bleeding is present; do not treat a major bleed with oral vitamin K alone. Identify interacting antibiotics and communicate why warfarin is temporarily withheld.
“I’ll ask questions that distinguish the causes.”

Assess duration and volume of bleeding, posterior bleed symptoms, airway compromise, dizziness/syncope, haemodynamic observations, other bleeding, indication for warfarin, previous INR, new antibiotics and medicines, alcohol and diet changes.
“There is a concern that needs checking.”

blocks.text: Patient says “Will I have a stroke if you stop my warfarin?” Explain short-term bleeding control and individualised restart plans. Give only history elicited by candidate; do not volunteer the diagnosis or investigation results.
Q1. What determines urgency? — Actual blood loss, airway/circulatory compromise and failure of local haemostasis, not INR alone.
Q2. What should happen to warfarin? — Withhold it while urgently assessing and correcting the high INR based on bleeding severity.

Q3. When is PCC indicated? — Major bleeding requiring emergency warfarin reversal: PCC 25–50 units/kg with vitamin K (phytomenadione) 5 mg IV. For non-major bleeding with a high INR, withhold warfarin and give vitamin K 1–5 mg IV (BSH).
Q4. What initial epistaxis measures? — Lean forward, sustained soft-nose compression, escalate to packing/cautery/ENT when necessary.
Q5. What after reversal? — Reassess bleeding and circulation, repeat INR and make a specialist-guided anticoagulation restart plan.

“The first decision is whether the patient needs emergency assessment now.”

“Before assuming that diagnosis, I should consider: Minor controllable nosebleed differs from major or life-threatening bleeding with instability, ongoing severe haemorrhage or critical-organ bleeding.”

“The specific action I must not omit is: Do not use an asymptomatic-INR algorithm when bleeding is present; do not treat a major bleed with oral vitamin K alone. Identify interacting antibiotics and communicate why warfarin is temporarily withheld.”

THINK: Warfarin-associated over-anticoagulation with active epistaxis; severity must be graded before choosing reversal. SAY: explain uncertainty clearly. DO: ABCDE and epistaxis control (sit forward, compress soft nose), FBC, repeat INR, group-and-save if significant, medication interaction review and ENT if persistent/posterior bleeding. NUMBERS: 20-minute consultation. TRAP: Do not use an asymptomatic-INR algorithm when bleeding is present; do not treat a major bleed with oral vitamin K alone. Identify interacting antibiotics and communicate why warfarin is temporarily withheld. FINISH: Withhold warfarin, control local bleeding and give vitamin K according to the relevant non-major bleeding pathway; an NHS regional guideline specifies 2 mg oral phytomenadione for non-major haemorrhage. If major/life-threatening bleeding, use emergency reversal with IV vitamin K plus four-factor PCC under local protocol and specialist input. Reassess INR and bleeding and plan safe anticoagulation resumption.
